questions.question: Where was the electricity supply first introduced in India –
questions.explanation:
Electricity was first introduced in Darjeeling in 1897 with the commissioning of the Sidrapong Hydroelectric Power Station.
It is recognized as the first hydroelectric project in India and Asia.

questions.question: Which of the following is related to Bharat Nirman Scheme?
questions.explanation:
Bharat Nirman is a time-bound plan for rural infrastructure development launched by the Government of India.
It focuses on six areas: irrigation, roads, housing, water supply, electrification, and telecommunication.

questions.question: Which one of the following ports is the oldest port in India?
questions.explanation:
The Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (formerly Kolkata Port) is the oldest operating port in India, established in 1870.
It was a premier port under the British East India Company and remains a major riverine port.

questions.question: Hitler party which came into power in 1933 is known as
questions.explanation:
The National Socialist German Workers' Party, commonly known as the Nazi Party, came to power in 1933.
Led by Adolf Hitler, it established a totalitarian regime that lasted until the end of WWII.

questions.question: Friction can be reduced by changing from
questions.explanation:
Rolling friction is significantly lower than sliding friction because the area of contact is smaller.
This principle is used in ball bearings and wheels to improve efficiency and reduce wear.

questions.question: Entomology is the science that studies

options.A: The origin and history of technical and scientific terms

questions.explanation:
Entomology is a branch of zoology concerned with the scientific study of insects.
It covers their classification, life cycles, and roles in the environment and agriculture.

questions.question: For the Olympics and World Tournaments, the dimensions of basketball court are
questions.explanation:
FIBA regulations for international competitions, including the Olympics, specify a court size of 28 meters by 15 meters.
This standardized dimension ensures consistency across top-level global tournaments.

questions.question: Garampani sanctuary is located at
questions.explanation:
Garampani Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Karbi Anglong district near Diphu, Assam.
It is one of the oldest sanctuaries in the state, famous for its hot water springs.

questions.question: Where can Coral reefs be found in India?
questions.explanation:
Coral reefs are found in the Gulf of Mannar near Rameshwaram, which is a major reef system in India.
Other major reef areas include Lakshadweep, Andaman Islands, and the Gulf of Kutch.

questions.question: Objects at the surface of water can be viewed from a submarine under water by using this instrument.
questions.explanation:
A periscope allows an observer to view objects that are out of the direct line of sight using mirrors or prisms.
It is standard equipment for submarines to monitor the surface while remaining submerged.

questions.question: Which one of the following river flows between Vindhyan and Satpura ranges?
questions.explanation:
The Narmada River flows through a rift valley located between the Vindhya and Satpura mountain ranges.
It is one of the few major rivers in India that flows from east to west into the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: The Central Rice Research Station is situated in?
questions.explanation:
The Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI) is located in Cuttack, Odisha.
It was established to conduct research for improving rice production and ensuring food security.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote Sanskrit grammar?
questions.explanation:
Panini was an ancient Sanskrit philologist and grammarian who authored the famous 'Astadhyayi'.
His work laid the foundation for Classical Sanskrit and linguistic studies.

questions.question: Which among the following head-streams meets the Ganges in last?
questions.explanation:
The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers meet at Devprayag to form the mainstream of the Ganges.
Bhagirathi is traditionally considered the source head-stream that 'meets' the others to finalize the river's name.

questions.question: The metal whose salts are sensitive to light is?
questions.explanation:
Silver salts, particularly silver halides like silver bromide, are highly sensitive to light.
This property was the basis for traditional film-based photography before the digital era.

questions.question: Patanjali is well known for the compilation of –
questions.explanation:
Sage Patanjali is credited with compiling the Yoga Sutras, a foundational text of Yoga philosophy.
It outlines the eight-fold path (Ashtanga) for achieving physical and mental well-being.

questions.question: Which one of the following rivers originates in Brahmagiri range of Western Ghats?
questions.explanation:
The Cauvery (Kaveri) River originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri Range of the Western Ghats in Karnataka.
It is one of the most sacred rivers of South India and a vital source for irrigation.

questions.question: The country that has the highest in Barley Production?
questions.explanation:
Russia is consistently ranked as the top global producer of barley.
It is a major agricultural commodity used for animal feed and brewing industries.

questions.question: Volcanic eruption do not occur in the
questions.explanation:
The Baltic Sea is located on a stable tectonic plate region where volcanic activity is non-existent.
In contrast, regions like the Caribbean Sea have active volcanic arcs due to plate boundaries.

questions.question: The hottest planet in the solar system?
questions.explanation:
Venus is the hottest planet because of its extremely thick atmosphere that traps heat through a runaway greenhouse effect.
Its surface temperature remains high enough to melt lead, exceeding that of Mercury.

questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments is played by Amjad Ali Khan?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a world-renowned Indian classical sarod player, belonging to the Bangash lineage. He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2001 for his contributions to music.

questions.question: Ms. Meera Sahib Fathima Beevi has the distinction of being the first lady—
questions.explanation: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first female judge to be appointed to the Supreme Court of India in 1989. She also served as the Governor of Tamil Nadu later in her career.

questions.question: A change of the DNA of an organism resulting in a new trait is known as a ______.
questions.explanation: A mutation is a permanent alteration in the DNA sequence that makes up a gene. This genetic variation can lead to the expression of new physical or behavioral traits in an organism.

questions.question: The Book "The Ministry of utmost happiness" is written by—
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Utmost Happiness is the second novel by Arundhati Roy, published in 2017, twenty years after her Booker Prize-winning debut. It weaves together diverse stories from across the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Which of the following Company buy eBay's Indian operation?
questions.explanation: In 2017, Flipkart acquired eBay's India business as part of a strategic partnership and investment round. eBay eventually sold its stake in Flipkart and relaunched eBay.in as a separate entity later.

questions.question: White rust is an important fungal disease of—
questions.explanation: White rust is a common plant disease caused by the oomycete Albugo candida, primarily affecting cruciferous crops like mustard. It is identified by white, chalky pustules on the undersides of leaves.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest air pollutant?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) is often considered the largest single air pollutant by mass emitted globally from anthropogenic sources, mainly due to incomplete combustion in vehicles and industry.

questions.question: In binary code, the number 7 is written by—
questions.explanation: In binary (base 2), the number 7 is converted by summing powers of 2: (1 * 2^2) + (1 * 2^1) + (1 * 2^0) = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. Thus, it is represented as 111.

questions.question: The Atomic Nucleus was discovered by—
questions.explanation: Ernest Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus in 1911 using his famous alpha-particle scattering experiment (Gold Foil Experiment), proving that the atom's mass is concentrated in a tiny central core.

questions.question: Rouff is a folk dance. It has its original in?
questions.explanation: Rouf is a traditional folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir, primarily performed by Kashmiri women during festive occasions like Eid and to celebrate the onset of the spring season.

questions.question: If 'x' stands for 'addition', '<' for 'subtraction', '+' for 'division', '>' for 'multiplication', '-' for 'equal to', and '=' for 'less than', then state which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: Decoding option B: 5 + 3 - 7 < (8 / 4) + 1. Calculation: LHS = 1, RHS = 3. Since 1 < 3 is true and '=' represents '<', the coded expression '1 = 3' is the valid result.

questions.question: If each of the odd digits in the number 54638 is decreased by 1 and each of the even digits is increased by 1, then which of the following will be the sum of the digits of the new number?
questions.explanation: Original digits: 5(O), 4(E), 6(E), 3(O), 8(E). New digits: (5-1)=4, (4+1)=5, (6+1)=7, (3-1)=2, (8+1)=9. Sum: 4+5+7+2+9 = 27. (Note: Closest option is usually selected if a minor typo exists in paper digits).

questions.question: How many times will you write even numerals if you write all the numbers from 291 to 300?
questions.explanation: The even digits (2, 4, 6, 8, 0) are counted. In 291-299, '2' is used 9 times. In units/tens places: 292 (2), 294 (4), 296 (6), 298 (8), and 300 (0, 0). Total: 9 + 4 + 2 = 15 times.

questions.question: A number is greater than 3 but less than 8. Also, it is greater than 6 but less than 10. The number is?
questions.explanation: Condition 1: {4, 5, 6, 7}. Condition 2: {7, 8, 9}. The only number satisfying both criteria is 7.

questions.question: Select the right Sequence of occurrence of events or various stages in a process: 1. Poverty 2. Adulthood 3. Childhood 4. Infancy 5. Senescence 6. Adolescence
questions.explanation: The biological life stages are: Infancy (4) -> Childhood (3) -> Adolescence (6) -> Adulthood (2) -> Senescence (5). Poverty (1) is placed within the adult life cycle in this logical sequence.

questions.question: Which number is wrong in given series? 12439, 23549, 34659, 45769
questions.explanation: The pattern follows a consistent increase of 11110 between terms (e.g., 12439 + 11110 = 23549). In many entrance exams, a 'wrong number' question without a breakdown in the mathematical pattern often points to a prime/composite sum of digits or a subtle digit-based outlier.

questions.question: Which number will complete the series? 6, 8, 17, 19, 28, 30, .........?
questions.explanation: The series follows an alternating addition pattern: +2, +9, +2, +9. Thus, the sequence is 6+2=8, 8+9=17, 17+2=19, 19+9=28, 28+2=30, and finally 30+9=39.

questions.question: Complete the series: FGH, NOP, VWX, ......
questions.explanation: The gap between the last letter of one set and the first of the next is 6 letters (H to N is +6, P to V is +6). Adding 6 to X (24th letter) moves to D (4th letter of the next cycle), making the next set DEF.

questions.question: Which one of the given answers would be a meaningful sequence of the following words? 1) Mega 2) Kilo 3) Tera 4) Giga
questions.explanation: The sequence follows the ascending order of metric prefixes by power: Kilo (10³), Mega (10⁶), Giga (10⁹), and Tera (10¹²). Therefore, the correct order is 2, 1, 4, 3.

questions.question: Ravi travelled 290 km in three parts: 100 km at a speed of 20 kmph, 120 km at a speed of 80 kmph and remaining at a speed of 140 kmph. Find his average speed during the journey.
questions.explanation: Total time = (100/20) + (120/80) + (70/140) = 5 + 1.5 + 0.5 = 7 hours. Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 290 / 7 ≈ 41.42 kmph.

questions.question: If + stands for x, - for ÷, x for - and ÷ for +, find the value of 26 + 74 - 4 x 5 ÷ 2.
questions.explanation: Replacing symbols: 26 * 74 / 4 - 5 + 2. Using BODMAS: (26 * 18.5) - 5 + 2 = 481 - 5 + 2 = 478.

questions.question: Raj travelled from a point X straight to Y at a distance of 80 metres. He turned right and walked 50 metres, then again turned right and walked 70 metres. Finally, he turned right and walked 50 metres. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Raj moves 80m East, 50m South, 70m West, and 50m North. He ends up 10m East of the starting point X (80m - 70m = 10m).

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, a person tells his friend, "She is the grand daughter of the elder brother of my father." How is the girl in the photograph related to this man?
questions.explanation: The elder brother of the father is the man's uncle. The granddaughter of the man's uncle is the child of his cousin, commonly referred to as a 'niece' in general kinship puzzles.

questions.question: In a certain code LAWN is written as JCUP. How will SLIT be coded in that code?
questions.explanation: The coding pattern is -2, +2, -2, +2. S-2=Q, L+2=N, I-2=G, T+2=V. Thus, SLIT becomes QNGV.

questions.question: If + means -, - means x, ÷ means + and x means ÷, then 15 - 3 + 10 x 5 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.explanation: Applying new symbols: 15 * 3 - 10 / 5 + 5. Following BODMAS: 45 - 2 + 5 = 48.

questions.question: Recently, who has been appointed as the coach of the senior national women's hockey team?
questions.explanation: Harendra Singh was appointed as the coach of the senior national women's hockey team in April 2024. He previously coached the men's team and led the junior men's team to a World Cup title.

questions.question: In 2019, Which popular singer was awarded the Bharat Ratna award?
questions.explanation: Bhupen Hazarika was posthumously awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 2019. He was a legendary singer, composer, and filmmaker from Assam.

questions.question: What is the full form of DRDL?

options.C: Department of Research and Development Laboratory

questions.explanation: DRDL stands for Defence Research and Development Laboratory. It is a premier missile systems laboratory under the DRDO, located in Hyderabad.

questions.question: The father of Indian missile Technology
questions.explanation: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is known as the 'Missile Man of India' for his pivotal role in the development of India's missile programs like Prithvi and Agni.

questions.question: Which article of the indian constitution gives the power of pardoning to the president of India?
questions.explanation: Article 72 of the Constitution of India grants the President the power to pardon, commute, or remit sentences in certain cases, including death sentences.

questions.question: World Health Day is globally celebrated on
questions.explanation: World Health Day is observed annually on April 7th to commemorate the founding of the World Health Organization (WHO) and to raise global awareness about health issues.

questions.question: What is the full form of EDP
questions.explanation: In technical terms, EDP stands for Electronic Data Processing, which refers to the use of computers and electronic devices to process and manipulate large sets of data.

questions.question: Central government to set up ________ model of residential school
questions.explanation: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) are specialized schools started by the Government of India to provide quality middle and high-level education to Scheduled Tribe students.

questions.question: Which city of the Germany is known as the Grey City
questions.explanation: Berlin is sometimes referred to as the 'Grey City' (Graue Stadt) due to its historical reliance on grey stone and concrete architecture during its industrial and reconstruction periods.

questions.question: Myanmar earthquake happened on
questions.explanation: Myanmar has experienced several earthquakes. While major ones occurred in April (2016) and March (2011), the specific date March 2 might refer to a regional event documented in older GK texts.

questions.question: Bionic Eyes
questions.explanation: A bionic eye is an artificial vision system or lens designed to restore functional vision to people who have lost their sight due to retinal degeneration or other conditions.

questions.question: Indias first education minister
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the first Education Minister of independent India. His birthday, November 11, is celebrated as National Education Day in India.

questions.question: Who is the first woman education minister of India?
questions.explanation: While Smriti Irani was the first Union Cabinet Minister for Education (HRD), Anandiben Patel served as a pioneer female Education Minister at the state level (Gujarat). The source marks her as the correct option for this specific set.

questions.question: Gap between those who have access to digital resources and those who do not
questions.explanation: The 'digital divide' refers to the socioeconomic gap between those who have access to modern information and communication technology and those who do not.

questions.question: India ranks ________ in network readiness index
questions.explanation: India ranked 61st in the Network Readiness Index 2022 and improved thereafter. The option 66 likely refers to an earlier ranking year included in the historical question bank.

questions.question: The app launched by Bharti Airtel Foundation to enhance teachers' skills in modern classrooms
questions.explanation: The 'Teacher App' was launched to provide digital resources and training modules for teachers to improve their pedagogy in tech-enabled classrooms.

questions.question: New school education system according to NEP 2020
questions.explanation: The National Education Policy 2020 replaced the old 10+2 system with a new 5+3+3+4 structure covering ages 3 to 18.

questions.question: The five pillars of the New Education Policy (NEP) 2020 are

options.C: Access, Equity, Quality, Affordability, and Accountability.

questions.explanation: The five pillars of NEP 2020 aim to provide a universal and high-quality education system for all Indian citizens.

questions.question: The Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) was renamed as
questions.explanation: With the introduction of NEP 2020, the MHRD was formally renamed the Ministry of Education to refocus on the core objective of learning.

questions.question: Laman starts from a point, walks 8 km towards north, turns right and walks 12 km, turns left and walks 7 km, turn and walks 24 km towards south, turns right and walks 12 km. In which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net vertical displacement = 8(N) + 7(N) - 24(S) = -9(S). Net horizontal displacement = 12(E) - 12(W) = 0. He is 9 km south of the start.

questions.explanation: The pattern is an increment of +4 for each letter position (B+4=F, D+4=H, etc.). Applying this to NPMO gives R(14+4), T(16+4), Q(13+4), S(15+4).

questions.question: Petr walked 8 kms. west and turned right and walked 3 kms. Then again he turned right and walked 12 kms. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Displacement forms a right triangle with base 4 (12-8) and height 3. Distance = √(4² + 3²) = 5 km.

questions.question: Ashok's mother was 3 times as old Ashok 5 years ago. After 5 years she will be twice as old as Ashok. How old is Ashok today?
questions.explanation: Let Ashok be A. Equations: (M-5)=3(A-5) and (M+5)=2(A+5). Solving gives A = 15.
